note: English narration for the hackathon submission video. `text` is shown as captions. Kokoro reads `kokoro` when present, otherwise `text`; Chatterbox and macOS say read `speak` when present. Durations come from the audio, so replacing a sentence's audio retimes the video.

sentences.text: Who decides what runs next in a self-driving lab?
Self-driving laboratories, or SDLs, automate experiments and use the results to choose what to test next.
sentences.speak: Self-driving laboratories, or S-D-Ls, automate experiments, and use the results to choose what to test next.

sentences.text: Language-model agents such as Coscientist and ACRA have already run robotic experiments.
sentences.kokoro: Language-model agents such as co-scientist and ACRA have already run robotic experiments.
sentences.speak: Language-model agents, such as Coscientist and Ackra, have already run robotic experiments.

sentences.text: Worldwide — from Canada's Acceleration Consortium to the US Genesis Mission and Japan's ARiSE programme — efforts are under way to build and scale SDL infrastructure.
sentences.kokoro: Worldwide — from Canada's Acceleration Consortium to the US Genesis Mission and Japan's Arise programme — efforts are under way to build and scale SDL infrastructure.
sentences.speak: Worldwide, from Canada's Acceleration Consortium, to the U.S. Genesis Mission, and Japan's Arise programme, efforts are under way to build and scale S-D-L infrastructure.

sentences.text: Cloud laboratories already let researchers share instruments remotely, without owning a lab.
As this grows, a single facility could run many experiments at once — hundreds of instruments, nearly a hundred robot arms, and a fleet of mobile robots moving samples between them.
sentences.speak: As this grows, a single facility could run many experiments at once: hundreds of instruments, nearly a hundred robot arms, and a fleet of mobile robots moving samples between them.

sentences.text: But scale doesn't make resources unlimited.
Instruments, robot arms, floor space and time are all finite, and experiments compete for the same equipment and transport.
Every lab needs a scheduler and resource manager — deciding what to install, and what to run first.
sentences.speak: Every lab needs a scheduler and resource manager, deciding what to install, and what to run first.

sentences.text: How do we know whether that decision-maker is any good?
We built LabOpsBench: a benchmark that runs an agent's decisions inside a simulated laboratory, with instruments, robot arms, mobile robots, queues and finite buffers.
sentences.speak: We built Lab Ops Bench: a benchmark that runs an agent's decisions inside a simulated laboratory, with instruments, robot arms, mobile robots, queues, and finite buffers.

sentences.text: It simulates operations — not chemistry.
sentences.speak: It simulates operations, not chemistry.

sentences.text: At time zero, the agent sees every unfinished job — including future arrivals, with dependencies and durations — plus the room layout and resource limits.
sentences.speak: At time zero, the agent sees every unfinished job, including future arrivals, with dependencies and durations, plus the room layout and resource limits.

sentences.text: It picks an equipment configuration from shared candidates and gives each job a priority.
The engine validates the decision, dispatches operations and moves the robots.
Every 1,800 simulated seconds, the agent can re-prioritise or request a permitted equipment exchange.
sentences.kokoro: Every eighteen hundred simulated seconds, the agent can re-prioritise or request a permitted equipment exchange.
sentences.speak: Every eighteen hundred simulated seconds, the agent can re-prioritise, or request a permitted equipment exchange.

sentences.text: The score is makespan — time until the last sample is unloaded.
sentences.speak: The score is makespan: the time until the last sample is unloaded.

sentences.text: Unfinished runs get no score.
To ground the workloads, we turned public LeMat-Synth annotations — synthesis procedures extracted from the literature — into eight scheduling templates.
sentences.speak: To ground the workloads, we turned public Le-Mat Synth annotations, synthesis procedures extracted from the literature, into eight scheduling templates.

sentences.text: They power fourteen scenarios, from small cells to a hall with 32 instruments, 32 arms and 64 jobs.
sentences.speak: They power fourteen scenarios, from small cells to a hall with thirty-two instruments, thirty-two arms, and sixty-four jobs.

sentences.text: Here are two agents on the same task: twelve jobs — six five-step chains and six single mixing jobs.
sentences.speak: Here are two agents on the same task: twelve jobs: six five-step chains, and six single mixing jobs.

sentences.text: GPT-6 Luna's plan: feed the oven pipeline first.
sentences.speak: G-P-T six Luna's plan: feed the oven pipeline first.

sentences.text: It ranks the long chains on top, keeps the layout, and pushes those chains through.
Jev gets exactly the same observation and candidates.
sentences.speak: Jev gets exactly the same observation, and candidates.

sentences.text: Instead of a fixed order, it keeps revising its ranking across seventeen decisions, mixing the two job types as the lab changes.
Same lab, same jobs — different strategies.
sentences.speak: Same lab. Same jobs. Different strategies.

sentences.text: We also built a web interface for every recorded run.
On this task, Luna finished in 8.27 hours, Jev in 8.33, and first-in-first-out took 12.6.
sentences.speak: On this task, Luna finished in eight point two seven hours, Jev in eight point three three, and first-in, first-out took twelve point six.

sentences.text: The best method changes by task: on compact lab layouts, Jev and a workload-aware algorithm beat Luna.
Click any result to replay it in 2D or 3D and step through each decision.
sentences.speak: Click any result to replay it in 2-D or 3-D, and step through each decision.

sentences.text: Playback only reads recorded engine events — it never changes the score.
sentences.speak: Playback only reads recorded engine events. It never changes the score.

sentences.text: Today, LabOpsBench scores time.
sentences.speak: Today, Lab Ops Bench scores time.

sentences.text: But future labs will need to weigh much more — scarce elements, electricity, water — in one combined decision.
sentences.speak: But future labs will need to weigh much more: scarce elements, electricity, water, in one combined decision.

sentences.text: LabOpsBench is a foundation for evaluating those trade-offs, and for testing our simulation against real laboratories.
sentences.speak: Lab Ops Bench is a foundation for evaluating those trade-offs, and for testing our simulation against real laboratories.
